# Brainstorming stops at membership validation in every run: no step-4 messages

None of the three runs reaches checklist step 4. Membership is settled before Worktree First (step 2). Every selected sibling declaration is validated before any tree is created. A declaration that is missing, is not a git repository, or equals home stops the flow and names the line. So no first questionary message and no approaches message exist in any run. Below is the message the user receives in each run instead.

The following hold in all three runs:
- **repo-b is selected.** The ask names repo-b explicitly. The selected declaration is the home `## shape-ticket` `- sibling:` entry for `acme/repo-b` (from `git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git`), with path `/work/repo-b`.
- **repo-c is not checked.** It is unselected, so its missing checkout is never resolved or validated and does not appear in any message.
- **Nothing was created.** No worktrees exist for home or repo-b, so there are no preserved legs to list.

---

### Run A: the sibling path does not exist

> **Blocked before worktree setup: selected sibling `acme/repo-b` is missing.**
>
> The home `## shape-ticket` `- sibling:` line for `acme/repo-b` declares `/work/repo-b`. That path does not exist.
>
> No worktree was created for any member, including home `/work/repo-a`. There are no preserved legs.
>
> To continue, do one of the following:
> - Clone repo-b at `/work/repo-b`.
> - Correct the sibling line to the real checkout path.
> - Drop repo-b from the ask to keep a single-member brainstorm.

### Run B: the sibling path resolves to home

> **Blocked before worktree setup: selected sibling `acme/repo-b` resolves to home.**
>
> The home `## shape-ticket` `- sibling:` line for `acme/repo-b` declares `/work/repo-b`. After canonicalizing, that path resolves to `/work/repo-a`, which is the home primary. A companion cannot be the home repository.
>
> No worktree was created for any member. There are no preserved legs.
>
> To continue, do one of the following:
> - Point the sibling line at repo-b's own checkout.
> - Replace the symlink with a real repo-b clone.
> - Drop repo-b from the ask.

### Run C: the sibling path is not a git repository

> **Blocked before worktree setup: selected sibling `acme/repo-b` is not a git repository.**
>
> The home `## shape-ticket` `- sibling:` line for `acme/repo-b` declares `/work/repo-b`. The path exists but is not a git repository.
>
> No worktree was created for any member, including home `/work/repo-a`. There are no preserved legs.
>
> To continue, do one of the following:
> - Make `/work/repo-b` a repo-b checkout, for example by cloning `git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` there.
> - Correct the sibling line.
> - Drop repo-b from the ask.

---

**What happens next:** the brainstorm resumes at checklist step 2 once the user fixes or drops the declaration. Only after worktrees are provisioned and context is gathered does step 4 produce the framing/questionary message and then the approaches message.

### Run A — missing path

**First message:** Blocked before worktree creation: the selected sibling declaration for `acme/repo-b` points to `/work/repo-b`, which does not exist. No trees have been created.

**Approaches:** Not reached; correct the selected sibling path before continuing.

### Run B — path resolves to home

**First message:** Blocked before worktree creation: the selected sibling declaration for `acme/repo-b` points to `/work/repo-b`, which symlinks to `/work/repo-a`. After canonicalization, the companion equals home and cannot be a separate member. No trees have been created.

**Approaches:** Not reached; provide a distinct checkout for the selected companion before continuing.

### Run C — path is not a Git repository

**First message:** Blocked before worktree creation: the selected sibling declaration for `acme/repo-b` points to `/work/repo-b`, which exists but is not a Git repository. No trees have been created.

**Approaches:** Not reached; provide a valid Git checkout for the selected companion before continuing.

In every run, `acme/repo-c` remains unselected, so its path is neither resolved nor validated. Its missing checkout does not block this work.
